title: The finite exceptional mate has the purity counit normalization
statement: Let P be a finite purity setting with coefficient prime ell and extension E. Let n,m be natural numbers with m <= n. Write N=P at level n+1 and M=P at level m+1, and Q_T for the actual quotient scalar extension from N to M. Let X,Y be separated finite-type P.field.k-schemes, f:X -> Y a separated finite-type morphism over that field, and K in D^b_ctf(Y,N.Ring). Use the standing exceptional functors G_N,G_M of [thm-pur-composition-coherence], support functors F_N,F_M and counits epsilon_N,epsilon_M of [def-pur-smooth-trace], and the quotient and scalar adjunction of [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts]. Let e:Q_X(G_N K) ~= G_M(Q_Y K) be the full inclusion of the specified invertible finite exceptional mate b of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] at K. Let q at G_N K be the scalar adjunct of F_N of the scalar unit followed by the canonical compact-support restriction comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Then q(G_N K) followed by F_M(e.hom) followed by epsilon_M(Q_Y K) equals Q_Y(epsilon_N(K)). No smoothness, nonempty-scheme or quotient-flatness assumption is required.

proof.text: At the positive exponents n+1 and m+1, form the full-subcategory object represented by K. The specified b of lem-coef-finite-exceptional is invertible; apply the full inclusion on X to its component to construct e. Its endpoints are definitionally the purity compositionExceptional endpoints at these levels. No arbitrary witness of an isomorphism is selected.

source.place: The specified right adjoint, canonical scalar comparison, and final two paragraphs identifying adjunction maps

proof.text: Take the counit equation of finite_exceptional at that object and apply the full inclusion. To identify the included counits, use AdjunctionNormalized from adjunction_existsUnique: expand fixedHom, cancel the fixedExceptionalIso right-adjoint comparison, and use the intrinsic realization unit/counit identities. The bounded-etale-origin input furnished by compositionInput_bounded makes the positive branch of smoothExceptionalCounit apply. Thus each included finite counit is the published smoothExceptionalCounit.

source.place: The specified right adjoint, canonical scalar comparison, and final two paragraphs identifying adjunction maps

proof.text: Expand supportMap into finiteImageIso inverse, the coefficient compact-support comparison, and finiteImageIso. Transport its open adjunction through the intrinsic realization; equality with sfIntrinsicOpenAdjunction follows from their sectionwise restriction-unit normalization and left-adjoint uniqueness. The proper comparison is the prescribed restriction/direct-image map on K-injective representatives. Pasting identifies this supportMap with the scalar adjunct of compact support of the scalar unit followed by sfCompactSupportRestriction.

source.place: The specified right adjoint, canonical scalar comparison, and final two paragraphs identifying adjunction maps

proof.text: Substitute the counit and compact-support identifications in the included equation, with associativity of composition. The finite scalar and full-subcategory functors have the displayed underlying morphisms, so the resulting equation is precisely the assertion, also at equal indices and on empty schemes.

from.place: Proof Steps 2 and 4: exceptional finite reduction and compatibility of the adjunction counit

lean.statement:
theorem finiteReductionExceptionalFiniteModel_counit
    (K : Scheme.proEtaleDerivedCategory Y (P.finiteReductionSetting (n + 1)
      (Nat.succ_pos n)).Ring)
    (hK : finiteTorConstructible P.coefficients.l P.extension (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Y K) :
    let N := P.finiteReductionSetting (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n)
    let M := P.finiteReductionSetting (m + 1) (Nat.succ_pos m)
    let red := N.finiteReduction (m + 1) (Nat.succ_pos m) (Nat.succ_le_succ h)
    let adj := N.finiteReductionAdjunction (m + 1) (Nat.succ_pos m) (Nat.succ_le_succ h)
    let c := @HasCompactification.compactification X Y f
      (hasCompactification_of_finiteType_over_field P.field.k X Y f)
    ((adj Y).homEquiv _ _).symm
        ((N.smoothCompactSupport f).map
            ((adj X).unit.app ((N.compositionExceptional f).obj K)) ≫
          (Scheme.sfCompactSupportRestriction c
            (N.finiteReductionRingHom (m + 1) (Nat.succ_pos m)
              (Nat.succ_le_succ h))).hom.app
            ((red X).obj ((N.compositionExceptional f).obj K))) ≫
      (M.smoothCompactSupport f).map
        (P.finiteReductionExceptionalFiniteModel n m h f K hK).hom ≫
      M.smoothExceptionalCounit f ((red Y).obj K) =
    (red Y).map (N.smoothExceptionalCounit f K)
